question.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3).\end{aligned}
$$

Normalize the  vector  $p(t)={t}^{2}-3t+4.$
question.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.
$$

Since $p(t)={t}^{2}-3t+4,$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=2,\,p(2)=2,\,p(3)=4
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),p(t)⟩ & =[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}+[p(3)]^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2} \\  & =4+4+16 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $p(t)$, we divide $p(t)$ by its norm $‖p(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{p(t)}{‖p(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}-3t+4}{2\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{12}({t}^{2}-3t+4)\end{aligned}
$$
